summary: These four test methods check the RobotPet charge method: that charging adds the amount given, that the battery never rises above 100 or falls below 0. Each test sets a known starting battery value, calls charge, then asserts the value that should result.

lines.text: Because we don't know what battery value a new pet starts with, the test sets one itself. Fixing a known starting point turns a guess into a repeatable test scenario.
With a start of 50 and a charge of 20, 70 is the only correct answer, so this single assertion proves the charge method adds exactly the amount asked for.
Charging 90 by 50 would give 140, which is deliberately impossible. This test is really exercising the battery setter, not the arithmetic in charge.
A negative charge drains the battery, so the same method covers both directions and 30 becomes 20.
Draining 10 by 50 must stop at 0 rather than going negative, which is the lower half of the protection the setter provides.
